newsitem.title: USA: GM names new information technology chief.
newsitem.headline: GM names new information technology chief.

text.p: General Motors Corp., taking another step to build up its internal information systems management, on Wednesday said it named Dennis Walsh as its chief information technology officer.

Walsh most recently served as president of Conservation Through Innovation, a Prescott, Arizona-based developer of software and hardware for control of heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems.

In his new capacity, he will head an organization responsible for information systems architecture and standards, operations management, software productivity and quality, electronic commerce, data management, tracking of emerging technologies and systems engineering.
He will report directly to Ralph Szygenda, GM's new vice president and chief information officer.

GM has been building up its internal information strategy and management capability since the 1996 split-off of Electronic Data Systems Corp, which had been GM's wholly owned supplier of information services. EDS remains a primary supplier to GM.
Before his tenure at Conservation Through Innovation, Walsh was vice president of information systems and chief information officer for Entergy Corp, a $6.3-billion, New Orleans-based utility.
